project.name: AEGIS
project.maturity: Research direction · project sketch · active development
project.tagline: From protocol descriptions to machine-checkable security obligations.
project.lead: AEGIS is a research direction for turning post-quantum IoT authentication and key-establishment protocols into structured framework models, a typed DSL, formal security games, and Lean 4 or Coq/Rocq proof obligations.

workflow.title: Protocol Submission
workflow.summary: Provide a protocol paper, structured description, pseudocode, message flow, or DSL.

workflow.title: Extraction and Normalization
workflow.summary: Identify parties, messages, credentials, algorithms, state, and claimed properties.

workflow.title: IoT-PQ-AKEmin Mapping
workflow.summary: Represent the protocol in a common minimal inspection model.

workflow.title: IoT-PQ-AKEgen Adapter
workflow.summary: Construct transcripts, contexts, freshness maps, and partnering rules.

workflow.title: Compatibility Checking
workflow.summary: Evaluate the protocol against structural requirements R1–R12.

workflow.title: DSL Generation
workflow.summary: Generate a typed and provenance-preserving specification.

workflow.title: DSL Validation
workflow.summary: Check syntax, types, protocol flow, state, and semantic consistency.

workflow.title: Security-Game Generation
workflow.summary: Instantiate selected AKE and IoT robustness experiments.

workflow.title: Formal Translation
workflow.summary: Translate definitions and theorem targets to Lean or Rocq.

workflow.title: Machine Checking
workflow.summary: Check proof terms, assumptions, placeholders, and counterexamples.

workflow.title: Final Report
workflow.summary: Produce a precise report with evidence, limitations, and artifacts.

requirements.title: Typed and domain-separated encoding
requirements.summary: Protocol fields, roles, versions, and labels must have unambiguous encodings.

requirements.title: Transcript completeness
requirements.summary: Every value affecting acceptance, authentication, algorithm selection, or key derivation must be represented.

requirements.title: Identity and peer binding
requirements.summary: The local identity and intended peer must be tied to the session context.

requirements.title: Credential binding
requirements.summary: Credential identifiers used for authentication must be bound.

requirements.title: Algorithm-suite binding
requirements.summary: Negotiated KEM, authentication, hash, KDF, and hybrid identifiers must be bound.

requirements.title: Role separation
requirements.summary: Initiator and responder contexts must be distinguishable.

requirements.title: Fresh contribution
requirements.summary: The session key must depend on session-specific fresh material.

requirements.title: Authentication binds the transcript
requirements.summary: Authentication material must cover the relevant transcript context.

requirements.title: Session-key derivation binds the transcript
requirements.summary: The KDF must combine key material with the required context.

requirements.title: Cheap pre-authentication checks
requirements.summary: Expose low-cost checks before expensive post-quantum operations.

requirements.title: State-update clarity
requirements.summary: State update timing, commit points, rollback, and recovery must be explicit.

requirements.title: Explicit failure behavior
requirements.summary: Failures must have clear rejection behavior and rejected sessions output no key.

core.title: Correctness
core.summary: Honest partnered sessions accept and agree on context and key.

core.title: AKE session-key secrecy
core.summary: A fresh session key is indistinguishable from a random key.

core.title: Mutual authentication
core.summary: An authentication-fresh accepted session has a unique matching peer session.

core.title: Forward secrecy
core.summary: Post-acceptance long-term compromise does not reveal past session keys.

core.title: KCI resistance
core.summary: Compromising one party does not enable impersonation of another party to the victim.

core.title: UKS resistance
core.summary: Parties do not share a key while disagreeing about peer identity or credential.

core.title: Replay resistance
core.summary: Old messages do not cause a new session to accept without a live matching execution.

core.title: Downgrade resistance
core.summary: Negotiation interference does not force an unauthorized weaker suite.

iot.title: State-reveal resilience
iot.summary: Parameterized by an explicit leakage profile Λ.

iot.title: Desynchronization resilience
iot.summary: Parameterized by disturbed-session bound q and recovery bound ρ.

iot.title: Energy-exhaustion resistance
iot.summary: Parameterized by a cost model and bound Γ.

verificationStatuses.title: Machine-checked
verificationStatuses.definition: The exact frozen theorem has a complete kernel-accepted proof without prohibited placeholders.

verificationStatuses.title: Machine-checked under assumptions
verificationStatuses.definition: The proof is accepted and depends on explicitly listed assumptions.

verificationStatuses.title: Structural certificate verified
verificationStatuses.definition: A structural property is machine-checked; this is not automatically a complete cryptographic theorem.

verificationStatuses.title: Open
verificationStatuses.definition: The statement is well-formed, but no complete proof is available.

verificationStatuses.title: Proof rejected
verificationStatuses.definition: A submitted proof was rejected; this does not show the theorem is false.

verificationStatuses.title: Blocked
verificationStatuses.definition: Required model information or backend support is missing.

verificationStatuses.title: Untrusted placeholder
verificationStatuses.definition: The apparent proof depends on a placeholder, hidden axiom, or unapproved dependency.

verificationStatuses.title: Formally refuted
verificationStatuses.definition: A checked proof of negation or valid checked counterexample exists.

verificationStatuses.title: Not applicable
verificationStatuses.definition: The property does not apply to the selected configuration.
